verdicts.title: get_str_from_p_as_int crashes on non-ASCII C strings (signed char -> chr() out of range)
verdicts.reasoning: Line 10 imports `char` from `numba.core.types`; verified at runtime that `numba.core.types.char` has repr `int8` and `.signed == True`. Line 255: `mem_view = carray(void_p, shape=(MAX_STR_LENGTH,), dtype=char)` — so each element is a signed int8. Line 259: `s += chr(char_as_code_p)` — any byte in 0x80..0xFF reads back as a negative value (e.g. 0xC3 -> -61), and `chr(-61)` raises `ValueError: chr() arg not in range(0x110000)` (confirmed by direct Python evaluation). The NUL-terminator check `== 0` on line 257 is unaffected since only 0x00 is zero; every continuation byte of a UTF-8 multi-byte sequence triggers the crash path. The finding's claim is accurate: the function is documented in CLAUDE.md as the canonical C-string reader (including for `sqlite3_errmsg`), making this a real correctness defect for any non-ASCII string data.
